questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language (English) and the courses available at the host university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, Deakin University had a fine set-up similar to kunet and Absalon where all the necessary information could be found.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange team at Deakin University held an informal information meeting for all exchange students with relevant information. I furthermore received help from Student Central (student councellers) and the exchange team to change one of my courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Three different housing options were available: shared apartment (4-6 persons in each), a study apartment (alone) or a dorm room (10-12 persons in each, not possible if older than 23 years).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The on campus housing offered dinner approximately once a week and then we had a kitchen to cook in. No kitchen equipment was available, so I had to purchase everything to cook with, including plates, utensils, pot, pans, etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus was a great way of getting to know a lot of people, both other exchange students, international students, and local students. The on campus accommodation arranged a lot of free introduction events to get people to socialize with each other which was a really nice way of meeting people. However, the apartments and rooms were very boring and sterile without charm. As Deakin University is located in a suburb to Melbourne, Burwood, the on campus housing was of course also located in Burwood right beside the uni so there was a 40-50 minutes tram ride into the city. No kitchen equipment, bed linen, duvets, pillows, etc. were provided so I had to purchase it myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As there is a housing crisis in Melbourne at the moment, it can be quite difficult to find housing off campus. The exchange students, I know, who lived off campus loved it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an email from Deakin University with a guide to register to my courses. First, I created a profile on DeakinSync (their kunet/Absalon) where I could register for my courses. Then I followed the guide and registered for the courses I wanted to online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Deakin University has a Student Central with student counsellors who can help with course registration and other stuff.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted successfully. After I had received my timetable, I got help from Student Central to change one of my classes from an on campus class to an online class (same course though).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's very easy and simple if you just follow the guides provided.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general, the academic level was not that great. The courses were, however, interesting, but the teachers didn't expect much of the students compared to UCPH.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one bachelors course (3rd year) which was very, very easy. I furthermore had three masters courses, two of them quite easy as well and the last one a bit harder.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very similar to UCPH with lectures and seminars. The grading system was, however, very different as the courses I study had assignments, quizzes, and/or presentations during the semester which all accounted for a percentage of my final grades. I only had an exam in one course, and the exam only accounted for 40% of my final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HSH323: Program Planning, Management and Evaluation (Bachelors course)
HSH703: Health Promotion
HSH719: Economic Evaluation 1
HSH766: Economics and Health Policy Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: HSH719: Economic Evaluation 1 if you're interested in economic evaluations in health care.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping and alcohol were more expensive than in Denmark while eating out was a bit cheaper than in Denmark. Otherwise, the prices were quite comparable with Danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sports clubs and other clubs at Deakin University.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any, but some of my friends were very happy about the outdoor club that arranged hikes, canoe trips, etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Prolonged weekend trip to Tasmania, weekend trip to Mornington Peninsula, Great Ocean Road, and/or Sydney. Driving along the east coast and/or west coast. 

Go to The Lume, ACMI and NGV (museums), stroll around in Fitzroy, eat croissants at Lune, drink drinks at Naked for Satan, eat ice cream from Piccolina.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as the Australian culture is very similar to the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living on campus makes it more probable to meet local students, otherwise to go to seminars and participate.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That Australians are very helpfull - also even when you don't ask them for help.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to be as much ahead of your studies (assignments especially) as possible as you'll be happy about having a lot of time to enjoy during the last weeks of your exchange. If you put in an effort, you'll pass all your courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of nice people who are now good friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to expressing myself in English all the time - especially in more difficult conversations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
